headline: India Glycols Limited: Receipt of NCLT Order
sum: India Glycols Limited received an NCLT order, disclosed to NSE on 20 August 2026; specific operative details (restructuring, merger, resolution plan, or insolvency outcome) not clarified in the bare announcement.
implication: The receipt of an NCLT order implies potential insolvency resolution under IBC, restructuring approval, or scheme sanction - practitioners must review the full order to identify statutory compliance obligations and timeline triggers.
detail: India Glycols Limited informed the NSE of receipt of a National Company Law Tribunal order on 20 August 2026. The announcement does not disclose whether this relates to insolvency resolution (IBC Ch. XI/Ch. V), a scheme of arrangement (CA 2013 s. 230–232), merger/amalgamation (CA 2013 s. 232), or another NCLT jurisdiction. The order's operative effect on the company's equity, creditor rights, stakeholder approvals and implementation timeline requires review of the full order.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) Ch. XI (Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process)
framework.note: Central; used if the NCLT order relates to admission, resolution plan approval or closure of an insolvency petition.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) Ch. V (Liquidation)
framework.note: Central if the order is a liquidation order following insolvency or rejection of resolution plans.
Central if the NCLT order sanctions a scheme of arrangement, merger or amalgamation.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, s. 441 (Compromises and Arrangements in Winding Up)
framework.note: Applies if the NCLT order relates to creditor composition in a winding-up proceeding.

framework.ref: NCLT Rules, 2016, r. 11–15 (Procedure: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process)
framework.note: Procedural rules for CIRP; track timelines and compliance obligations.

framework.ref: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, s. 13 (SARFAESI)
framework.note: Applicable if secured creditors initiated proceedings prior to NCLT referral.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India Master Direction on Resolution of Stressed Assets, 2016
framework.note: Relevant if the NCLT order concerns resolution of RBI-regulated financial assets or loan restructuring.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, s. 60 (Preferential Transactions)
framework.note: Review for avoidance actions or unwinding of pre-insolvency transactions by the IP.

conditions: Parties' receipt and review of the full NCLT order text (not disclosed in announcement).
If insolvency-related: discharge of obligations under approved resolution plan or liquidation protocol.
If scheme-related: member/creditor approval per s. 230–232, CA 2013.
approvals: Pending review: Company/member approval (if scheme-based), regulatory confirmations (RBI/sectoral regulator, if any)

triggers.law: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, s. 31 (CIRP Duration)
triggers.note: If CIRP-based, the 180/270-day timeline for resolution plan approval or closure is now critical.
If scheme-based, the NCLT sanction triggers filing with MCA/ROC and implementation obligations.

triggers.law: NCLT Rules, 2016, r. 18 (Implementation of Resolution Plan)
triggers.note: Post-approval, the IP and successful resolution applicant must comply with implementation timelines.

firms.note: Bar & Bench article does not identify legal counsel or party advisors.
